newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended one percent higher on Monday morning at a new record close, just off an intra-day high set earlier in the day.
The market shrugged off the negative sentiment of gains by the French left wing in the first round of general elections which afflicted bonds and the dollar.
"There are still buyers in the Netherlands. Funds must invest their money," one trader said.
The AEX index of leading shares rose 8.23 points, or 1.02 percent, to 812.19. Earlier in the afternoon, it reached a new intra-day high of 812.87.
The rise was, however, largely the result of the strength of market heavyweight Royal Dutch and the financial sector.

Royal Dutch shares gained 5.50 guilders to 373.50. Dealers said the positive feeling was partly a carry-over from meetings with analysts and partly reflected a forward view of the four-for-one share split due at the end of June.
"It gave some interesting news to analysts," one trader said.
Financial stocks were also firmer. ABN AMRO gained 50 cents to 36.80 while ING rose by 2.70 guilders to 88.80 and Fortis Amev by 2.30 guilders to 82.20.
The latter report first quarter figures later this week.
Traders said the gains were the result of healthy expectations on the upcoming results and also of the hardened perception that interest rates would not rise.
"There's quite some positive interest rate sentiment," one trader said.

One of the largest gainers, meanwhile, was ASM Lithography, maker of semi-conductor production equipment. Its shares rose 6.30 guilders to 103.60, partly in parity gains with the U.S. where technology stocks rose.

As for overall market sentiment, chartists were more upbeat than last week, when some saw the uptrend running out of steam. This week, with some reservations, most saw clearer upward signals with next resistance for the AEX at around 825 points.
"All in all, we return to a mildly bullish stance with an intermediate objective around 825," ING Barings said.
